objective: Close service-media replacement, superseded-object cleanup and abandoned-draft cleanup lifecycle without reopening browser authority.
risks: Browser can update or delete owner storage objects without a server transaction that also reconciles service_media and service_versions.
A replaced object has no canonical superseded state or retention window.
Abandoned draft media has no explicit expiry authority.
Cleanup cannot prove that an object is unreferenced by approved, pending or historical service versions before deletion.
requiredClosure: Introduce explicit server-side media lifecycle operations behind JWT-verified Edge authority.
Separate upload reservation from promotion into an approved or pending service version.
Track active, pending, superseded and cleanup-eligible media states canonically.
Remove direct browser UPDATE and DELETE authority for service-media objects.
Guarantee reference-safe cleanup across services, service_media and service_versions.
Add deterministic runtime, structural and SQL validation gates.
Validate only in staging before documentary closure.
nextControlledWork: Design the canonical media lifecycle schema and server operations, then implement the smallest reversible candidate without touching production.
